newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Philip Morris evacuates two officials from Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris evacuates two officials from Moscow.

text.p: U.S. tobacco group Philip Morris Companies Inc has evacuated two Moscow-based British staff and their families after they received threats, a company official said on Friday.
"We can confirm that two employees and their families were flown out of Russia as a precautionary measure after a threat was received," said Andrew White, director of corporate affairs in Moscow.
"We have notified the authorities and they're taking appropriate action to resolve this issue," he said.
He said the officials and their families were flown out on Wednesday night. He declined to give details of the threat.
Although threats and murders against Russian businessmen have become commonplace in the wild atmosphere of post-Soviet capitalism in Russia, incidents against Western businessmen are relatively rare.

But in November last year Paul Tatum, part owner of one of the city's most prominent hotels, was shot dead near the building's entrance. An American reporter investigating the case also left the country within hours after he was threatened.
White said the evacuation on Wednesday was the first of its kind for Philip Morris.
About two thirds of Russian men smoke and a third of its women, making the country an important market for Philip Morris, which has invested in cigarette factories across the former Soviet Union.
